mechanism: Once-daily oral, selective allosteric activator of red blood cell pyruvate kinase-R (PKR). PKR activation is intended to reduce 2,3-diphosphoglycerate, increase ATP, improve hemoglobin-oxygen affinity, reduce sickle hemoglobin polymerization/sickling, and improve red blood cell survival.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists the assigned HIBISCUS2 study (NCT06612268) as a recruiting global Phase 3 randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled trial in 408 adolescents and adults with sickle cell disease, with actual start February 17, 2025, estimated primary completion August 27, 2027, and estimated study completion March 12, 2029. Novo Nordisk announced positive topline results from the pivotal HIBISCUS Phase 3 trial and plans first regulatory submission in the second half of 2026; no FDA approval was identified.
clinical_summary: HIBISCUS2 is designed to confirm whether etavopivat reduces adjudicated vaso-occlusive crisis (VOC) events with medical contact over 52 weeks, with secondary measures including Hb response greater than 1 g/dL at Week 24, time to first VOC, fatigue, hemoglobin, hemolysis markers, and 6-minute walk distance. Novo Nordisk's pivotal HIBISCUS topline announcement reported that etavopivat 400 mg once daily reduced annualized VOCs by 27%, prolonged median time to first VOC to 38.4 weeks versus 20.9 weeks for placebo, and produced Hb response greater than 1 g/dL at Week 24 in 48.7% versus 7.2% with placebo. Phase 1 SCD data showed proof of mechanism and Hb improvement, but detailed Phase 3 safety and subgroup data remain pending.
safety_summary: Novo Nordisk reported that etavopivat appeared well tolerated in HIBISCUS, with topline safety in line with previous etavopivat trials. In the published Phase 1 SCD study, 400 mg once daily for 12 weeks was described as well tolerated; adverse events were mostly Grade 1/2 and consistent with underlying SCD, five serious adverse events occurred in the open-label cohort, and vaso-occlusive pain episode was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event. HIBISCUS2 excludes recent voxelotor/similar agents, recent selectin antagonists such as crizanlizumab, regular transfusion therapy or frequent recent transfusions, strong CYP3A4 inducers, prior cellular therapy, significant hepatic dysfunction, and other high-risk features.
management_tools: Specialty pharmacy prior authorization if launched as a chronic oral therapy
Confirm sickle cell disease diagnosis/genotype and age per final label
Require documented baseline VOC history and medical-contact VOC burden before initiation
Require baseline hemoglobin and transfusion history documentation
Step requirement or documentation of inadequate response, intolerance, or contraindication to hydroxyurea where clinically appropriate and label-consistent
Quantity limit aligned to labeled tablet strength and once-daily dosing
Drug interaction edits for strong CYP3A inducers if supported by final label
Non-concomitant use policy with duplicative SCD disease-modifying agents such as selectin antagonists or HbS polymerization agents if label and evidence support restrictions
Continuation criteria requiring reduced VOC frequency, delayed/reduced healthcare utilization, Hb response, reduced transfusion burden, or other label-supported clinical benefit
Monitoring criteria for liver tests, hemoglobin overshoot, transfusion needs, and adverse events once final prescribing information is available
evidence_gaps: Full Phase 3 HIBISCUS results, adverse-event tables, discontinuation rates, subgroup analyses, and concomitant standard-of-care details are not yet published.
HIBISCUS2 is still recruiting and has no posted ClinicalTrials.gov results.
No FDA label, approved indication, final dosing, launch date, or direct etavopivat price is available.
Annual cost estimate uses Adakveo and Pyrukynd analog pricing; actual etavopivat pricing could differ materially.
Oxbryta's 2024 withdrawal underscores the need to scrutinize longer-term safety and VOC outcomes for new SCD disease-modifying therapies.

sources.title: A Study to Evaluate How Well Etavopivat Works in People With Sickle Cell Disease
supports: Assigned asset identity, sponsor, indication, and HIBISCUS2 acronym.
Recruiting Phase 3 randomized, quadruple-masked, placebo-controlled parallel trial in adolescents and adults with sickle cell disease.
Estimated enrollment 408; actual start February 17, 2025; estimated primary completion August 27, 2027; estimated completion March 12, 2029.
Primary endpoint is number of adjudicated VOC events with medical contact from baseline to Week 52.
Secondary endpoints include Hb response greater than 1 g/dL, time to first VOC, PROMIS fatigue, hemoglobin, LDH, reticulocytes, indirect bilirubin, and 6-minute walk distance.
Eligibility includes age 12 or older, confirmed SCD genotype, 1-15 documented VOCs in prior 12 months, and screening Hb 5.0-10.0 g/dL.
Key exclusions include recent voxelotor/similar agent, recent selectin antagonist, regular or frequent transfusion, strong CYP3A4 inducer use, prior cellular therapy, and hepatic dysfunction.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: A Study of Etavopivat in Adults and Adolescents With Sickle Cell Disease (HIBISCUS)
supports: Related pivotal HIBISCUS Phase 2/3/Phase 3 trial in adults and adolescents with sickle cell disease.
Active, not recruiting; enrollment 450; actual start January 29, 2021; estimated primary completion February 6, 2026; estimated completion March 19, 2027.
Phase 3 interventions included etavopivat 400 mg once daily, etavopivat 200 mg once daily, placebo, and selected-dose etavopivat.
Primary endpoints include hemoglobin response rate at 24 weeks and annualized VOCs at 52 weeks.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: A Research Study Looking at Long-term Treatment With Etavopivat in People With Sickle Cell Disease or Thalassaemia
supports: Related FLORAL long-term Phase 3 extension for etavopivat in sickle cell disease or thalassaemia.
Recruiting; enrollment 480; actual start January 10, 2025; estimated primary completion and study completion December 30, 2030.
Primary outcomes are treatment-emergent adverse events and adverse reactions up to Week 316.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.

sources.title: A SAD/MAD to Assess the Safety, PK/PD of FT-4202 in Healthy Volunteers and Sickle Cell Disease Patients
supports: Completed Phase 1 first-in-human etavopivat/FT-4202 study in healthy volunteers and sickle cell disease patients.
Enrollment 130; primary outcomes included adverse events and pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics.
No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted, but peer-reviewed Phase 1 SCD results have been published.

sources.title: Etavopivat is the first in a new class of drugs to successfully meet both co-primary endpoints in the phase 3 HIBISCUS trial, substantially reducing vaso-occlusive crisis events and improving haemoglobin response in sickle cell disease
supports: Novo Nordisk announced HIBISCUS topline Phase 3 results for once-daily oral etavopivat in adults and adolescents with sickle cell disease.
HIBISCUS met both co-primary endpoints: reduction in VOCs and improvement in Hb response versus placebo.
Etavopivat 400 mg reduced annualized VOCs by 27% versus placebo and prolonged median time to first VOC to 38.4 weeks versus 20.9 weeks.
Hb response greater than 1 g/dL at Week 24 was 48.7% with etavopivat versus 7.2% with placebo, adjusted rate difference 41.2%.
Topline safety was described as well tolerated and in line with previous etavopivat trials.
Novo Nordisk plans first regulatory submission for etavopivat in the second half of 2026.

Company describes etavopivat mechanism, FDA Fast Track/Rare Pediatric Disease/Orphan Drug designations, European orphan designation, acquisition through Forma Therapeutics, and HIBISCUS2/FLORAL program context.
Company states SCD affects around 8 million people worldwide, approximately 100,000 in the United States, and approximately 110,000 in Europe.

sources.title: 7807 Hibiscus2- A research study to evaluate how well Etavopivat works in people with sickle cell
supports: UK HRA summary confirms HIBISCUS2 title, sponsor Novo Nordisk A/S, EudraCT/EMA identifier 2023-509175-16, and ClinicalTrials.gov identifier NCT06612268.
Research summary describes etavopivat as a small molecule intended to activate a red-blood-cell protein involved in energy production and oxygen binding.
First 52 weeks assign participants to daily etavopivat or placebo; second 52 weeks participants take daily etavopivat.
Study is expected to include 408 adolescents and adults older than 12 years with SCD worldwide, with 1-15 VOCs in the past year and anemia.
Research Ethics Committee gave favorable opinion on August 30, 2024.

sources.title: Multicenter, phase 1 study of etavopivat (FT-4202) treatment for up to 12 weeks in patients with sickle cell disease
supports: Peer-reviewed Phase 1 SCD publication registered to NCT03815695.
Etavopivat is described as an investigational once-daily oral selective erythrocyte PKR activator.
Thirty-six SCD patients were enrolled across single-dose, multiple ascending dose, and open-label cohorts.
Open-label cohort received etavopivat 400 mg once daily for 12 weeks; 14 of 15 completed treatment.
ATP increased and 2,3-DPG decreased, supporting proof of mechanism.
Mean maximal Hb increase was 1.6 g/dL and 11 of 15 patients achieved Hb increase greater than 1 g/dL during treatment.

Adverse events were mostly Grade 1/2 and consistent with underlying SCD; five serious adverse events occurred in the open-label cohort; vaso-occlusive pain episode was the most common treatment-emergent adverse event.

sources.title: FDA Is Alerting About The Voluntary Withdrawal Of Oxbryta (voxelotor)
supports: FDA alerted patients and health care professionals that Oxbryta was voluntarily withdrawn from the market due to safety concerns.
FDA stated health care professionals should stop prescribing Oxbryta and patients should contact their health care professional about stopping and starting another treatment option.
Pfizer withdrew Oxbryta, ceased distribution, and discontinued active clinical trials and expanded access because recent data indicated benefit did not outweigh risks in SCD.

sources.title: DailyMed - ADAKVEO (crizanlizumab) injection
supports: SCD VOC-reduction analog.
Adakveo is indicated to reduce frequency of VOCs in adults and pediatric patients aged 16 years and older with SCD.
Recommended dose is 5 mg/kg by IV infusion at Week 0, Week 2, and every 4 weeks thereafter.
Dose is supplied as 100 mg/10 mL single-dose vial.

Warnings include infusion-related reactions and platelet-count interference; common adverse reactions include headache, arthralgia, nausea, back pain, fatigue, abdominal pain, pyrexia, diarrhea, vomiting, and oropharyngeal pain.

sources.title: DailyMed - PYRUKYND (mitapivat) tablet, film coated
supports: Oral pyruvate kinase activator analog.
Pyrukynd is a pyruvate kinase activator indicated for hemolytic anemia in adults with PK deficiency.
Dosing starts at 5 mg twice daily and titrates to a maximum recommended dose of 50 mg twice daily, with 56-tablet packs representing 28 days.
Warnings include acute hemolysis with abrupt interruption or discontinuation, hepatocellular injury in another condition, and CYP/UGT/P-gp interaction considerations.
Most common adverse reactions and laboratory abnormalities include estrone decreased in males, increased urate, back pain, estradiol decreased in males, and arthralgia.

supports: Agios lists Pyrukynd WAC of $25,760.00 for 5 mg, 20 mg, and 50 mg tablet products.

sources.title: Prior Authorization Criteria - Adakveo and Endari
supports: SCD payer-policy analog for VOC-reducing drugs.

Adakveo initial criteria include confirmed SCD diagnosis, at least 2 pain crises in the last 12 months, hydroxyurea use at maximum tolerated dose or medical reason not to use, current weight documentation, FDA-approved dose, and hematology/specialist prescribing.
Adakveo initial approval may be up to 6 months; reauthorization may be 12 months and requires reduction in pain crises, increased time between crises, or decreased days hospitalized.

Endari criteria similarly require SCD diagnosis, at least 2 crises in the last 12 months, hydroxyurea trial/compliance or medical reason, FDA-approved dose, and reauthorization attestation of reduced sickle cell crises.

sources.title: Pyrukynd (mitapivat) Prior Authorization with Quantity Limit Program Summary
supports: Oral pyruvate kinase activator payer-policy analog.
Policy applies prior authorization and quantity limit to Pyrukynd.
Quantity limit for Pyrukynd tablets is 56 tablets per 28 days.
Initial approval criteria require confirmed PK deficiency hemolytic anemia by genetic or enzyme testing criteria and no labeled contraindications, with 6-month initial approval.

Renewal requires prior approval, clinical benefit such as hemoglobin increase or decreased transfusion burden, specialist prescribing or consultation, and no labeled contraindications, with 12-month approval.

expected_launch_window.method: Derived from Novo Nordisk's stated plan for first regulatory submission in H2 2026, positive pivotal HIBISCUS topline data, FDA expedited/orphan designations, and typical post-filing review plus launch timing. HIBISCUS2 and FLORAL remain ongoing and may support label, confirmatory, or long-term safety evidence.
expected_launch_window.explanation: If the H2 2026 submission is filed and accepted without major delay, first approval and launch could plausibly occur in 2027; a 2028 launch remains plausible if review, data presentation, pediatric/adolescent issues, or manufacturing/label negotiations extend timing.

annual_cost_range.method: Low estimate uses SCD VOC-reduction analog Adakveo: 70 kg patient x 5 mg/kg = 350 mg, rounded to four 100 mg single-dose vials per infusion; first-year dosing at Week 0, Week 2, then every 4 weeks equals 14 infusions; 14 x 4 vials x $2,403.93 = $134,620. High estimate uses oral pyruvate kinase activator analog Pyrukynd: WAC $25,760 per 56-tablet/28-day package x 13 28-day periods = $334,880.
annual_cost_range.explanation: Etavopivat has no disclosed price. The range triangulates between an existing SCD VOC-reduction biologic and an oral pyruvate kinase activator rare-hematology analog, excluding rebates, discounts, dispensing/admin fees, wastage beyond rounded vials, adherence gaps, monitoring, hospital costs, and cost offsets from reduced VOCs or transfusions.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted oral once-daily first-in-class PKR activation, positive pivotal dual endpoint performance on VOC and Hb response, proof-of-mechanism Phase 1 data, SCD unmet need after Oxbryta withdrawal, and limited currently available disease-modifying options against incomplete published Phase 3 details and a 27% top-line VOC reduction.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Etavopivat could be meaningfully differentiated because it pairs oral chronic dosing with both VOC reduction and Hb improvement. A High rating is premature until full Phase 3 efficacy, safety, subgroup, discontinuation, transfusion, and concomitant-therapy data are available.

budget_impact.method: Combined high analog annual cost, chronic oral dosing, potentially broad SCD eligibility beginning at age 12, U.S. prevalence around 100,000 cited by Novo Nordisk, and likely uptake pressure after positive Phase 3 data and Oxbryta withdrawal.
budget_impact.explanation: Even though SCD is rare, chronic branded therapy at SCD/rare-hematology analog prices could create high per-treated-member spend and material plan impact, partly offset if VOCs, transfusions, emergency visits, or admissions decline.

disruption_risk.method: Assessed near-term regulatory-submission plan, positive pivotal topline results, oral administration, first-in-class mechanism, active Phase 3b/extension program, and the need to update SCD policy pathways after Oxbryta withdrawal.
disruption_risk.explanation: Etavopivat is no longer an early watchlist asset; plans should prepare coverage criteria, sequencing, quantity limits, and continuation logic before a potential 2027 launch.

recommended_action.method: Matched action to positive pivotal Phase 3 topline data, H2 2026 planned submission, ongoing Phase 3b/extension evidence generation, high analog cost, and likely need for plan criteria before launch.
recommended_action.explanation: Begin draft utilization-management criteria now, then finalize after full Phase 3 presentation/publication, FDA filing acceptance, label, dosing, safety monitoring, and price are available.

quality_flags: Assigned trial NCT06612268 is HIBISCUS2, a Phase 3b-style confirming/extended study that remains recruiting; launch timing is driven mainly by the separate pivotal HIBISCUS trial NCT04624659 and Novo Nordisk's H2 2026 submission plan.
No FDA approval or marketed etavopivat product was identified as of the 2026-05-28 check.
Full HIBISCUS Phase 3 results are currently company-reported topline data, not yet a full peer-reviewed Phase 3 publication.
No direct etavopivat price was found; annual cost estimate uses Adakveo and Pyrukynd analogs.
Oxbryta was withdrawn in 2024 due to safety concerns, so payer and clinical review should scrutinize long-term SCD outcome and safety evidence before broad coverage.
